articles.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Its Fast Model for Agentic Work
articles.excerpt: Hydrogen takes the execution tier of the Gemini 4 family: faster than the old Flash line, priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, and now running inside Google Search for all users.
articles.nri_angle: Indian developers and IT teams are among the heaviest users of Google's AI stack; a cheaper, faster execution model changes the cost math for agent-based development work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ISRO Test-Fires Revised PSLV Third Stage After Two Flight Anomalies
articles.excerpt: The strengthened PS3 solid motor was successfully ground-tested at Sriharikota on November 12 after anomalies on PSLV-C61 and PSLV-C62; ISRO says further tests will follow a detailed review of the data, and has not declared the vehicle ready to fly.
articles.image_caption: A solid motor fires during a ground static test at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. ISRO tested the revised PSLV third stage on November 12 after anomalies on two earlier missions.
articles.nri_angle: The PSLV is the vehicle that has carried many of the Indian and commercial satellites diaspora-linked startups and universities fly; its return to flight depends on this qualification sequence.

articles.title: Google's November Pixel Drop Brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10
articles.excerpt: Rambler, multi-step task automation and proactive suggestions reach last year's flagships, alongside a $29.99 Pixel Tag tracker and a smarter Call Screen for the Pixel 11.
articles.image_caption: A Google Pixel phone stands on a shelf, showing its rear camera bar and Google logo. The November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10 series.
articles.nri_angle: Multi-step Gemini automation in this Drop is available in India as well as the UK and Japan, and conversation summaries now include Hindi, making the update directly relevant to diaspora Pixel owners and their families in India.

articles.title: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao Holds Stake Calculated at About $703 Million Ahead of IPO
articles.excerpt: Moneycontrol's calculations from Anthropic's IPO filing put CFO Krishna Rao's stake at about $703 million, or roughly Rs 6,500 crore. The filing itself lists Rao, 43, with 9,497,900 shares beneficially owned, mostly in stock options, the largest holding of any non-founder.
articles.nri_angle: Rao's roughly Rs 6,500 crore calculated stake makes the Indian-origin CFO one of the most prominent diaspora figures in the AI industry's largest listings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jay Puri Among Names Reported in Nvidia Succession Talk as Board Backs Huang
articles.excerpt: Nvidia has named no successor to Jensen Huang and its board says it backs him during an independent investigation, but AP reporting cited by Inshorts lists former worldwide sales chief Jay Puri, CFO Colette Kress, chief scientist Bill Dally and co-founder Chris Malachowsky among possible frontrunners if the board ever acts.
articles.nri_angle: Puri's presence on the reported frontrunner list puts an Indian-origin executive at the centre of the succession question at the world's most valuable chip company, though Nvidia has named no successor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah Pledges Simpler App, Stronger AI Help
articles.excerpt: In his first detailed note in the job, Kunal Shah sets three priorities — simpler voice, groups and video, everyday tasks finished inside a chat, and AI that tracks bookings and appointments — with no launch dates yet.
articles.nri_angle: WhatsApp group chats, voice notes and video calls are the main daily link between diaspora families and relatives in India, so Shah's simplification and AI plans directly affect how those families communicate.

articles.title: German AI Chip Startup Sparxity Closes Series A, Total Funding Reaches $90 Million
articles.excerpt: The Dresden company formerly known as SpiNNcloud builds chips that skip unnecessary calculations in AI models. Lockheed Martin Ventures and GlobalFoundries joined the round, whose own size was not disclosed.
articles.image_caption: A Sparxity multi-rack computing system in a data centre. The Dresden company has closed a Series A round that brings its total funding to $90 million.
articles.nri_angle: A global AI-hardware story for technology readers tracking alternatives to GPU-only inference; no direct diaspora angle.

articles.title: DeepMind's AI Formally Verifies Key Signal Protocol Guarantees in Four Weeks
articles.excerpt: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code produced mathematical proofs for several of the Signal protocol's core security guarantees, found no new flaws in the parts it examined, and correctly failed older versions with known bugs. The work did not cover the whole Signal app, and Google will not say what it cost.
articles.image_caption: An illustration shows a user surrounded by digital security and shield symbols. Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verified key guarantees of the Signal protocol, which secures Signal, WhatsApp and Google Messages.
articles.nri_angle: The Signal protocol also underpins WhatsApp, the default messaging app for most Indian diaspora families; an independent mathematical proof of its guarantees is directly relevant to the privacy of those everyday conversations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China's Proposed Solar Tech Export Curbs Expose India's Dependence on Factory Machinery
articles.excerpt: Beijing's draft catalogue would prohibit or restrict exports of 12 solar manufacturing technologies, from perovskite cells to polysilicon processes, with public comment open until November 15. The products India buys would keep flowing; the machinery and know-how to make them at home are what is being gated.
articles.image_caption: Rows of solar panels stretch across a solar farm under a clear sky. China's proposed export controls target the manufacturing technology and machinery behind panels like these, not exports of finished modules.
articles.nri_angle: India's solar build-out, and the PLI factories meant to supply it, still run on Chinese equipment and process know-how; gating that layer affects project timelines and costs across the Indian energy sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stanford's Fingernail-Sized Chip Untangles Mixed Light Into Clean Beams
articles.excerpt: A silicon photonic chip has, for the first time, taken partially coherent light from multiple lasers and sorted it into separate, pure beams — work published in Nature Photonics that could sharpen microscopy and astronomy.
articles.image_caption: Gloved hands hold the circuit board carrying the photonic device on an optical bench. The Stanford-led chip separated partially coherent light from multiple lasers into pure, independent beams.
articles.nri_angle: A Stanford-led advance in photonic chips, a field where Indian-origin engineers and researchers are heavily represented in US laboratories, with NASA already testing astronomical uses.

articles.excerpt: Gaia data show the cluster catalogued as one system is a 21-million-year-old cluster and a 562-million-year-old cluster that passed within 23 light-years about 6 million years ago.
articles.image_caption: The Pleiades (M45), an open star cluster, in a file photograph. An Indian-led team found the cluster catalogued as UBC 63 is two clusters that survived a close flyby.

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora gamers who grew up riding these highways, a Delhi-NCR built from real map data — dhabas, truck art and all — is the draw; the wishlist is open now ahead of the 2027 release and a demo.
